Since \(y=\frac{x^2}{4}\), the second distance is
\[
\left|\frac{x^2}{4}+2\right|=\frac{x^2}{4}+2.
\]
For the first distance, note
\[
-\frac34x^2+4x-7<0
\]
for all \(x\), because its discriminant is \(16-21=-5<0\) and the leading coefficient is negative. Thus
\[
\left|4x-3y-7\right|
=\left|-\frac34x^2+4x-7\right|
=\frac34x^2-4x+7.
\]
So
\[
D(x)=\frac15\left(\frac34x^2-4x+7\right)+\frac{x^2}{4}+2
=\frac25x^2-\frac45x+\frac{17}{5}.
\]
This quadratic is minimized at
\[
x=\frac{4/5}{4/5}=1.
\]
Then
\[
D(1)=\frac25-\frac45+\frac{17}{5}=3.
\]
\[
\boxed{3}
\]
